clue.text: S. American beast finds a better state in retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to better something is to cap or top it
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana, a US state

explanation.surface: A South American animal finds life improves once it stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reads the run backwards: ACAPLA turned round. 'better' is the verb, to cap or top.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated camelid of the Andes, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Topless actress not acting in trees

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Swedish film actress
not acting means genuine, real

explanation.surface: A topless actress, no longer performing, up in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in or relating to trees.

clue.text: Standard to see Charles perhaps, receiving bust lip

indicators.note: receiving means the royal word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Charles was long the Prince of Wales, so he is an example of a prince

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of lip are jumbled

explanation.surface: Seeing Prince Charles with a split lip is the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' makes IPL from LIP, which PRINCE takes in by 'receiving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral rule or standard of behaviour.

clue.text: Players on pitch

explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a play form its company, and to pitch something is to throw or fling it.

clue.text: Dupe — one's hand in it a bloomer?

parts.note: to fox someone is to fool or dupe them
a cryptic description of a glove, which a hand goes inside

explanation.surface: A dupe gets caught red-handed in a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowers is jokingly a bloomer; the tall spiky purple flower is a classic garden one.

clue.text: Opportunity for maiden

explanation.definitionFit: A chance or gap is a way in, and a maiden voyage or speech is the first, inaugural one.

clue.text: Monster writer wants some thing with veins

parts.note: a Gorgon is a snake-haired monster of Greek myth
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A monstrous author wants a slice of something veined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thing with veins' is a blue-veined cheese, not a body.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian blue cheese, streaked with mould.

clue.text: Late notice given about right course for heavenly body

indicators.note: the notice is put round the right piece, enclosing it

parts.note: an obit is a notice of someone late, deceased

explanation.surface: A belated warning about the correct path for a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: The path a planet or moon follows around another body.

clue.text: Fit for consumer, though belied by a different construction

indicators.note: a different construction of the same letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food fit to eat, though its look belies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe or suitable to eat.

clue.text: Protect from wearing Chanel?

parts.note: Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer
wearing something means having it on

explanation.surface: Dressing in Chanel as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: COCO (Chanel's first name) then ON for 'wearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up snugly and shield, as a larva is shielded in silk.

clue.text: Sulphur most disastrous in salt water

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for salt water

parts.note: brine is salty water

indicators.note: something disastrous is wrecked, so the letters of most are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sulphur is at its worst when dissolved in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' makes MSTO from MOST, which goes 'in' BRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old biblical name for the element sulphur, as in fire and brimstone.

clue.text: Religious teacher detailing the beast

indicators.note: de-tailing, cutting off the tail or last letter of the word for the beast

parts.note: a rabbit is a small furry beast

explanation.surface: A religious teacher describes the animal in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailing' looks like describing fully; read it as de-tailing, removing the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish scholar and teacher of religious law.

clue.text: Career people

explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, and a people or ethnic group is also called this.

clue.text: Flat in Ritz with hooligan not one good for development

indicators.note: not says some letters are to be left out of the pool before it is rearranged
development means building something new out of the letters of the two words

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A flat in the Ritz shared with a lout is hardly suitable for property development.
explanation.walkthrough: From the letters of RITZ and HOOLIGAN take away I ('one') and G ('good'), as 'not' asks; 'for development' rearranges the remaining ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying level, parallel to the ground, as opposed to vertical.

clue.text: Biscuit in roll filled with hot swan's wings

indicators.note: filled with means the bread roll encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
hot can mean lustful, randy

indicators.note: wings are the two edges, so only the first and last letters of swan are taken

explanation.surface: A bread roll with hot swan's wings in it.
explanation.walkthrough: BAP is a British soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often cream-filled.

clue.text: Almost hopeful, given tablet

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: someone hopeful of success is aspiring

explanation.surface: Someone nearly hopeful is handed a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling pill.

clue.text: Stare at lad briefly in garden feature

parts.note: to gaze is to stare

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word for a lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Ogle a young man for a moment by the garden summerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open-sided summerhouse built for the view.

clue.text: What will make the earth move for male, one asleep

definitions.text: What will make the earth move

parts.note: a bull is a male animal
someone dozing is a dozer

explanation.surface: Romance hint: what makes the earth move for a man is falling asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make the earth move' plays on the romantic phrase; literally it is a machine shifting soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy tracked vehicle that pushes soil about.

clue.text: Dog on track is mine

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A dog on the railway line is mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive; it is a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit with its buildings.

clue.text: Note singer offered to the audience

indicators.note: something offered to an audience is heard, so the word for a singer is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A singer gives a musical note to the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music, but it is a banknote: a TENNER is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British name for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Bloody taste of Welsh food

parts.note: rare meat is bloody
a taste is a small bit

explanation.surface: A bloody morsel of Welsh cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Melted cheese on toast, also called Welsh rabbit.

clue.text: Astronomer sees endless wind before one constellation

indicators.note: endless cuts the last letter off the word for a wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
the Roman numeral for one is I
Leo, the Lion, is a zodiac constellation

explanation.surface: A stargazer watches a gale blow before picking out one star pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who first turned a telescope on the heavens.

clue.text: Treat house-buyer badly? Doctor admits extremes with little hesitation

indicators.note: admits means the doctor lets the other pieces in

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a doctor
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet
um is a small hesitating sound

explanation.surface: A doctor lets in all comers with barely a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: In British house sales a seller who accepts a higher offer after agreeing one has done this to the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the price after agreeing a sale cheats the buyer.

clue.text: Counter revolutionary transport in Australia

indicators.note: in means the turned piece goes inside the Australia abbreviation
revolutionary means turned round, so cab is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Counter-revolutionary transport running in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter revolutionary' reads as one idea; split it so 'Counter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads used for counting.

clue.text: What loser may get by advertising single during drink

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the middle of the drink word, so it encloses them

parts.note: booze is alcoholic drink
PR stands for public relations, publicity
I, the numeral one, is single

explanation.surface: A consolation prize is awarded during a drinks promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke award for whoever comes last in a contest.

clue.text: Bulb lit, one lit

parts.note: a light that is lit is on
the Roman numeral for one is I
a light that is lit is on

explanation.surface: A light bulb glows, then another lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' is the vegetable, not a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable bulb with pungent layers.

clue.text: Superstar won't lift a finger, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is taken for how it sounds

parts.note: someone who won't lift a finger is idle

explanation.surface: A celebrity is too lazy to do anything, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A star worshipped by fans.

clue.text: One flying at night from Earth to Mars, upwards

indicators.note: upwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something flies at night from Earth to Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points inside 'Earth to', and 'upwards' reads HTOM back up the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-flying insect related to butterflies.

clue.text: Prison harbouring Irish dog

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail is sheltering an Irish hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog is not Irish but a Scottish terrier; 'Irish' only gives IR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rough-coated Scottish terrier.

clue.text: Con given the cane at last by member, endlessly

parts.note: bamboo is the cane plant
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: endlessly cuts the last letter off the word for a member

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A convict is caned and finally given a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives Z, the final letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To con is to trick or hoodwink someone.

clue.text: Shows contempt about joiner in children's play areas

indicators.note: about means the contempt word wraps round the joiner

parts.note: spitting is a show of contempt
the word and joins words together

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a carpenter in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter; here it is the conjunction AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxes of sand in parks where small children dig.

clue.text: Fruit of that girl wrapped in blubber

indicators.note: wrapped in means the girl word goes inside the weeping word

parts.note: to blubber is to cry
her refers to that girl

explanation.surface: A girl sobbing over a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' suggests whale fat; it is the verb to sob.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round red stone fruit.
